headline: B2GOLD BEATS Q1 — $1.2B REVENUE, $539M OPERATING CASH FLOW, ALL FOUR MINES OUTPERFORMED GUIDANCE
snippet: B2Gold (TSX: BTO) posted Q1 2026 net income of $200M ($0.15/share) and adjusted net income of $260M ($0.19/share) on $1.2B in revenue — all four producing mines exceeded production expectations at a consolidated AISC of $1,964/oz versus gold realised near $4,700/oz. The company declared a Q2 dividend of $0.02/share and repaid its $75M revolving credit balance in April. Earnings call held May 9.

headline: McEWEN MINING FLIPS FROM $6M LOSS TO $33M PROFIT — Q1 REVENUE DOUBLES AS HIGH GOLD PRICE HITS INCOME STATEMENT
snippet: McEwen Mining (TSX: MUX) swung from a Q1 2025 net loss of $6.3M to Q1 2026 net income of $33.4M ($0.56/share) as revenue jumped 107% to $74M on 30,471 gold-equivalent ounces — a 26% production improvement year-over-year. The company is self-funding growth toward 250,000–300,000 GEO/year by 2030 while the Los Azules copper project advances toward a construction decision.

headline: BARRICK REPORTS Q1 MONDAY — ANALYSTS EXPECT 111% EPS SURGE AS RECORD GOLD TESTS OPERATING LEVERAGE
snippet: Barrick Mining (TSX: ABX) reports Q1 2026 results before market open Monday, May 11. Analysts forecast $0.74 EPS on $4.76B revenue — a 111% year-over-year earnings jump — with the stock already up 7% in anticipation. The central question: whether Barrick's operational improvements translate record gold prices into genuine margin expansion, or whether cost inflation absorbs the windfall.

headline: LUNDIN GOLD DRILLS 667 G/T AU OVER 7.5M AT FRUTA DEL NORTE — TWO HIGHEST GRADE-THICKNESS HOLES EVER AT FDN
snippet: Lundin Gold (TSX: LUG) released two bonanza-grade holes at Fruta del Norte South (Ecuador): 667.78 g/t Au over 7.50m and 523.01 g/t Au over 8.25m — the two highest grade-thickness intercepts ever drilled at the mine. A record $85M exploration budget and 17 active rigs are targeting a 133,000-metre 2026 program focused on extending FDNS and FDN East.

headline: GOLD SEEKER ISSUE 72: MINERS HOLD KEY SUPPORT LEVELS — WHAT CATALYST WILL BREAK GDX OUT OF ITS RANGE?
snippet: GoldSeek's week-of-May-4 mining roundup finds gold and silver holding critical technical levels after a period of consolidation following Q1 highs. GDX recently broke above the $42–$46 resistance zone and gold miners surged 6.16%, while silver miners (SIL ETF) posted 6.56% — setting up a potential breakout if a macro catalyst materialises.

headline: GOLDMINING INC. LAUNCHES 2-RIG DRILL AT SÃO JORGE, BRAZIL — 8,000-METRE TAPAJÓS GOLD PROGRAM UNDERWAY
snippet: GoldMining Inc. (TSX: GOLD) has commenced a two-rig, 8,000-metre exploration drill program at its 100%-owned São Jorge gold project in Brazil's prolific Tapajós gold district, Pará State. The program targets a resource expansion at a project located in one of South America's most active junior gold exploration belts.

headline: CAMECO BEATS Q1 THEN SIGNS $2.6B INDIA URANIUM DEAL — 22 MILLION LBS LOCKED IN FROM 2027 TO 2035
snippet: Cameco (TSX: CCO) reported Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $509M, up sharply year-over-year, on stronger uranium volumes and realised prices. Separately, the company announced a nine-year, $2.6B uranium supply agreement with India's atomic energy agency covering 22 million pounds of deliveries from 2027 through 2035 — underscoring the flight to long-term supply security among growing nuclear states.

headline: MINING M&A HITS $21.6B IN Q1 2026 — STRONGEST DEAL QUARTER SINCE 2023 AS SUPPLY-CHAIN LOGIC DRIVES CONSOLIDATION
snippet: Global mining M&A reached $21.6B across 121 transactions in Q1 2026 — the strongest opening quarter since 2023 — as producers prioritise securing critical-mineral supply chains over organic growth. White & Case notes 32% of respondents expect strategic partnerships to dominate deal structures in 2026, a shift from outright acquisitions in previous cycles.

headline: 2 MINING STOCKS ANALYSTS ARE BUYING THIS MONTH — GOLD ABOVE $4,700 AND COPPER AT RECORDS MAKE THE CASE
snippet: Motley Fool analysts identify two diversified miners with strong free-cash-flow profiles and dual leverage to gold and copper as both metals hold historically elevated prices in May 2026 — arguing that mining equities are still catching up to the underlying commodity rally, making the current relative underperformance a buying opportunity.

headline: COPPER FLIRTS WITH ALL-TIME HIGH AT $6.25/LB — AI DATA CENTRES AND GRID BUILD-OUT CREATE STRUCTURAL DEMAND FLOOR
snippet: Copper reached $6.25/lb on May 8 — up 8.8% over one month and 35.7% year-over-year — as investors price in sustained long-term demand from AI infrastructure, power grid modernisation, and clean energy build-out. Unlike recent supply-disruption price spikes, analysts point to structural demand as a durable floor for prices, supporting exploration spending in copper-focused junior projects.
